solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Production of ideal responses renders one inhuman

indicators.note: a production is something made up out of raw material, so the letters that follow are worked into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written: fourteen letters of raw material

explanation.surface: Giving only model answers turns a person into something robotic.
explanation.definitionFit: To depersonalise is to strip away individuality, which is a way of making someone seem less than human.

clue.text: Somehow, I muffle ultraviolet emission

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put together in an order not given

blocks.note: taken as written
UV is the standard abbreviation for ultraviolet

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have somehow dampened the ultraviolet given off by a source.
explanation.definitionFit: An effluvium is an unpleasant vapour or discharge given off by something, so it is an outflow or emission.

clue.text: Finish off unrestricted deal backing option

indicators.note: without restrictions means without its bounds, so the word loses both its end letters
backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from its last letter to its first

blocks.note: deal with its outer letters removed
a put is an option to sell shares at a set price

explanation.surface: A trader wraps up a deal that has no conditions, falling back on an option.
explanation.walkthrough: In finance a put (option) gives the right to sell at a fixed price; fitting for a Financial Times puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat up is to consume completely, an idiom for finishing something off entirely.

clue.text: Impact of drug trafficking measure?

blocks.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
a bump is a knock or impact

explanation.surface: A question about how effective a policy against drug smuggling has been.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trafficking' suggests drug dealing, but read it as traffic: a measure to slow cars. 'Impact of drug' puts the drug first, as in drug-impact.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed bump is a raised ridge across a road, a traffic-calming device that forces vehicles to slow.

clue.text: He's wandering, though patently sane

blocks.note: plainly sane means there is clearly no madness, split into a two-word phrase

explanation.surface: Someone drifts about aimlessly, yet seems perfectly in their right mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Wandering suggests a confused mind, which the second half denies; the answer splits as NO + MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a person who roams from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: Something to drive pirate underground?

blocks.note: read as under + ground: ground and land are synonyms, and in a down entry what sits under it follows it
a rover is an old word for a pirate or sea robber

explanation.surface: A vehicle that might chase a buccaneer into hiding below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' reads as one word but splits into under + ground. Land Rover is a British make of four-wheel-drive vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Land Rover is a rugged off-road car, so it is a thing one drives.

clue.text: Raise hell after husband's scratched new car

indicators.note: scratched means struck out, so that letter is removed from the word
in a down entry raising something lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: Hades is the underworld
H is the abbreviation for husband, and it is the letter taken out
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone kicks up a fuss once the husband has scraped the new car.
explanation.walkthrough: Hades without its H gives ADES, which turned upward gives SEDA; N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan is a saloon car, the usual American word for an enclosed four-door car.

clue.text: FT probes pay out put on hold

indicators.note: a probe pushes into something, so this goes inside the other word

blocks.note: to spend is to pay out money
the Financial Times, the setter's own paper, refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: Financial Times investigations into payouts are delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appears in the FT, so the paper can name itself as US.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to halt it temporarily, which is putting it on hold.

clue.text: Spirit of old king not half apparent

indicators.note: not half means only one half remains, so the second half of the word is dropped

blocks.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
taken as written before it is halved

explanation.surface: The spirit of a former monarch is only partly visible, like a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a ghost, but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape residue, a strong alcoholic spirit.

clue.text: Restore relations with whistleblower

blocks.note: a referee blows a whistle
IT is a coy word for sex, as in sexual relations

explanation.surface: Someone tries to mend family ties with a person who exposed wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistleblower' suggests an informant, but it is a match official.
explanation.definitionFit: To refit a ship or building is to overhaul and restore it to working order.

clue.text: Dreadful trio managed D minus and three Es

indicators.note: managed means handled or arranged, so the letters are organised afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
three copies of the letter

explanation.surface: Three poor students scraped a D minus and three E grades.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a school report.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eumenides are the three Furies of Greek myth, terrifying avenging goddesses, hence a fearsome threesome.

clue.text: Chubby head regularly flopped

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: plump means chubby
the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A tubby boss kept collapsing into a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump down is to drop or sit heavily, so plumped means flopped.

clue.text: Abandoned garden on verge of complete disorder

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and uninhibited, so these letters run wild
a verge is an edge, here the final edge of the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A neglected garden is on the edge of total chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' looks like neglect, but here means unrestrained; 'disorder' is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into confusion, so it is a verb meaning to disorder or upset.

clue.text: Basis of argument in Times article about tax haven

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the pair of words before it is read backwards

blocks.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
a is the indefinite article
the Isle of Man, a British low-tax jurisdiction

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about an offshore tax refuge lays out the premise of a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper; it is the multiplication sign. IOM is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as true and used as a starting point for reasoning.

clue.text: Sage losing heart at Epiphany's beginning to improve

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle part of the word is removed
a beginning is a start, so only the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: Melchior is one of the three wise men of the Nativity story
taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A wise man loses heart on the feast of the Epiphany yet tries to do better.
explanation.walkthrough: Epiphany is the feast marking the Magi's visit, which makes the surface apt. Melchior loses CH, its two middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To meliorate is a formal verb meaning to make or become better, from Latin melior.

clue.text: Imprudent one in Rome contrived to dispose of ecstasy

indicators.note: disposing of something gets rid of it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: una is Italian for one (feminine)
devised means contrived or worked out
E is slang for the drug ecstasy, and it is the letter taken out

explanation.surface: A reckless Roman schemed to get rid of some drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadvised means acting without due thought or counsel, so rash and unwise.

clue.text: Outstanding material not primarily employed rashly for fuel

indicators.note: not means without, so the letters picked out are taken away from the word before
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters of the next words count

blocks.note: ace means excellent or outstanding
Terylene is a polyester fabric
the first letters of each word, the pair that is removed

explanation.surface: A superb fabric is used without proper thought for a purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Terylene, a British brand name for polyester fibre, loses an E and an R to give TYLENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetylene is a flammable gas burnt in welding torches and lamps, so it serves as a fuel.

clue.text: Put up with this type of clue or throw in the towel?

blocks.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
this clue is a down clue

explanation.surface: A solver wonders whether to endure clues like this or give up.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to itself: it sits in the down list.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is to withdraw or resign, and throwing in the towel is an idiom for giving up.

clue.text: Sort of multiple shooting that accelerates progress in screening?

definitions.text: Sort of multiple shooting that accelerates progress in screening?

blocks.note: surface reading: a series of gunshots, perhaps a shooting spree
setter's reading: a camera taking many frames at intervals so that slow change speeds up when shown on screen

explanation.surface: It sounds like a burst of gunfire that hurries things along during a security check.
explanation.walkthrough: Shooting means filming and screening means showing on a screen; a plant growing or clouds moving appear fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-lapse photography takes frames at long intervals, so on playback slow processes appear greatly sped up.

clue.text: Stuff for bed that beats lubricant

blocks.note: to top something is to beat or surpass it
oil is a lubricant

explanation.surface: Something for the bedroom that outdoes ordinary lubricant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests a bedroom, but it is a garden flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsoil is the fertile upper layer of earth, the material spread on a garden bed.

clue.text: Studied accountancy — ultimately to make money

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is used

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone trained as an accountant in the end to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for cash, as is 'readies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready, usually as 'the ready', is informal British slang for money available to spend.

clue.text: Too much talk arising from Margaret Taylor

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters sit inside the words that follow
in a down entry arising means going upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: letters spanning the two names

explanation.surface: Someone named Margaret Taylor is causing a lot of chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yatter is informal for incessant idle chatter, so it means talk in excess.

clue.text: Instrument displaying little capacity to disrupt horseplay?

indicators.note: to disrupt something is to break into it, so these letters are inserted into the word

blocks.note: polo is a game played on horseback, so play on horses
one cubic centimetre, I being Roman one and cc the abbreviation, a tiny volume

explanation.surface: A musical instrument shows little ability to break up rough games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horseplay' means rowdy fun, but the question mark lets it be play on horses. Fittingly, piccolo is Italian for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A piccolo is a small high-pitched flute, a woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Pass over cycling article without note

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the word drops those letters
cycling means going round, so letters move from the front to the back of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
ti (te) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A biker passes over a newspaper piece that has no footnote.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTICLE without TI is ARCLE; moving AR from front to back gives CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a hurdle or bar is to get over it without touching, so to pass over it.

clue.text: Head's two points shy of 111

indicators.note: shy of means short of, so the named letters are missing

blocks.note: two compass points, both east, the letters removed
the digits read as one, I (Roman one), one

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a number just short of one hundred and eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 111 is read as one + I + one, and each ONE loses an E.
explanation.definitionFit: Onion is old slang for the head, as in 'off one's onion' meaning out of one's mind.

clue.text: Earliest date for constructing Spooner's prized vessel?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

blocks.note: a dear (prized) yacht, said yot; swapping the opening sounds gives the phrase

explanation.surface: A boatbuilder dates the oldest prized ship he built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Year dot' is British idiom for the very beginning, as in 'since the year dot'.
explanation.definitionFit: The year dot is an informal British phrase for the very earliest time imaginable.

clue.text: Community leader — a baronet — in bad odour? The opposite

indicators.note: in normally means the first item goes inside the second
the opposite flips the nesting just stated, so the second item goes inside the first instead

blocks.note: taken as written
Bt is the abbreviation for baronet
BO is body odour, a bad smell

explanation.surface: A local figure, a titled gentleman, is out of favour, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In bad odour' is a real idiom for being disliked, which disguises the instruction. A baronet is the lowest British hereditary title.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of a monastic community of monks.

clue.text: Effective fusion, at last, of music dramas from east and west

indicators.note: reading from the east means from right to left, backwards in an across entry
fused at the last letter means the end of one and the start of the other merge, so one shared letter is dropped

blocks.note: an opera is a music drama, read from the west, left to right
Evita is a stage musical, read from the east

explanation.surface: An effective blend of musical theatre from Asia and the West.
explanation.walkthrough: The two music dramas are an opera and Evita; the second reads backwards, and the two share their joining A.
explanation.definitionFit: Operative means in force and producing its intended effect, as an operative clause is.

clue.text: Bankrupt fellow changed sides

indicators.note: switching sides swaps left for right, so an L is replaced by an R

blocks.note: bloke is British slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A ruined man switched political allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) becomes R (right) in BLOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Broke is informal for having no money, which a bankrupt person has.

clue.text: Retaining steel used for section of canal

indicators.note: used can mean worked over or exploited, so the letters are put to a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An engineer uses steel to shore up a stretch of waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canal' suggests a waterway; it is the alimentary canal, the digestive tract.
explanation.definitionFit: The large intestine is the lower part of the alimentary canal, the gut running from mouth to anus.
